title: WPMS/2070/2013 of Lalita Prasad Shah AND ANOTHER Vs Smt Shanti Devi AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 2070 of 2013 (M/S)
Lalita Prasad Shah & another Ö...Petitoners.
Versus
Smt. Shanti Devi & others ....Respondents.
Present:
Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. Ganesh Kandpal, Advocate for the respondents.
Honíble Alok Singh, J. (Oral)
 An application under Section 21 (1)(a) of U.P. Act No. 13
of 1972 was filed by landlord/petitioner, herein, before the Prescribed
Authority, seeking eviction of the tenant/respondents, herein, on the
ground of bona fide need of the landlord saying that earlier the
property in question was joint property of the landlord as well as of
his brother and in the partition, the property in question came to the
share of landlord/petitioner, herein. The landlord/petitioner, herein,
needs residential accommodation. He will demolish existing structure
and shall raise new construction. Thereafter, landlord shall live
therein. Application so moved by the landlord/petitioner, herein, was
allowed by the Prescribed Authority. However, appeal filed by the
tenant was allowed by the Appellate Authority, vide judgment dated
13.06.2013, on the ground that instead of moving the application
under Section 21 (1)(a) of the Act, landlord ought to have moved an
application under Section 21 (1)(b) of the Act.
 If landlord requires the building for his personal use after
demolition and reconstruction, application is very well maintainable

under Section 21 (1)(a) of the Act, however, if he wants to demolish
the property and wants to reconstruct it not for his personal use and
occupation then, of course, he may file an application under Section
21 (1)(b) of the Act. Since, in the present case, landlord sought
release of the building for his personal use, therefore, application
under Section 21 (1) (a) was very well maintainable.
 Mr. Ganesh Kandpal, learned counsel appearing for the
tenant/respondents, submits that he has been instructed by the
tenant/respondents to furnish undertaking to the effect that
tenant/respondents shall handover peaceful vacant possession of the
property in question to the landlord on or before 30.9.2016.
 With the consent of learned counsel for the parties,
present petition, thus, stands disposed of in the following terms.:
(i) Release application moved by the landlord/petitioner,
herein, stands allowed. Impugned judgment passed by the
learned Appellate Court dated 13.6.2013 stands set aside.
Property in question stands released in favour of the
landlord/petitioner, herein.
(ii) Tenant/respondents, herein, shall handover peaceful
vacant and actual possession of the property in question to the
landlord/petitioner, herein, on or before 30.9.2016.
(iii) Tenant/respondents, herein, shall pay the entire
arrears of the rent on or before 15.10.2014 and shall pay the
mesne profit at the rate of agreed rent till actual physical

possession is handed over to the landlord from today. Mesne
profit shall be paid on or before 10th day of each and every
month.
(iv) Undertaking to the above effect shall be furnished
before the Prescribed Authority in the shape of affidavit of the
tenant/respondents, herein, on or before 15.10.2014.
(vi) If the undertaking is not furnished or arrears are not
paid till 15.10.2014 or any default is made in the payment of
monthly mesne profit, landlord shall be entitled to evict the
tenant/respondents, herein, forthwith with the help of the police
at the cost and risk of the tenant/respondents, herein.
 No order as to costs.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
 15.9.2014
Avneet
